tax.text: Income Taxes . In determining taxable income for financial statement reporting purposes, we must make certain estimates and judgments. These estimates and judgments are applied in the calculation of certain tax liabilities and in the determination of the recoverability of deferred tax assets which arise from temporary differences between the recognition of assets and liabilities for tax and financial statement reporting purposes. We regularly assess the likelihood that we will be able to recover our deferred tax assets. Unless recovery is considered more-likely-than-not (a probability level of more than 50%), we will record a charge to income tax expense in the form of a valuation allowance for the deferred tax assets that we estimate will not ultimately be recoverable or maintain the valuation allowance recorded in prior periods. When considering all available evidence, if we determine it is more-likely-than-not we will realize our deferred tax assets, we will reverse some or all of the existing valuation allowance, which would result in a credit to income tax expense and the establishment of an asset in the period of reversal.

ocf.heading: Operating Activities
ocf.text:
Our working capital cash inflows and outflows from operations consist primarily of cash collections from our customers, payments for inventory purchases and payments for employee-related expenditures.

Net cash provided by operating activities of continuing operations was $6.5 billion in 2025, primarily due to our net income of $4.3 billion in 2025, adjusted for non-cash adjustments of $4.6 billion and net cash outflows of $2.4 billion from changes in our operating assets and liabilities. The primary drivers of the changes in operating assets and liabilities included a $2.2 billion increase in inventory primarily to support the continued ramp of Data Center products in advanced process technology nodes. Net cash provided by operating activities of the ZT Manufacturing Business, classified as discontinued operations, was $1.2 billion.

Net cash provided by investing activities of discontinued operations in 2025 was $1.3 billion, primarily from the sale of the ZT Manufacturing Business.

gp.heading: Gross Margin
gp.text: Gross margin was 54% and 52% for the three months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively, where the increase was driven by a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue. Gross margin was 54% and 47% for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 and September 27, 2025, respectively, where the increase was driven by the absence of inventory and related charges associated with the U.S. government export control on AMD Instinct MI308 Data Center GPU products that was recorded in the prior year period and a favorable product mix, including higher Data Center segment revenue.

oi.text: Operating income for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was $2.8 billion compared to operating income of $1.3 billion for the prior year period. The increase in operating income was due to higher gross profit, partially offset by higher operating expenses. Net income for the three months ended September 26, 2026 was $2.4 billion compared to net income of $1.2 billion for the prior year period. The increase in net income was primarily driven by higher operating income.

rd.heading: Research and Development (R&D) Expenses
rd.text: R&D expenses of $2.8 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 increased by $0.7 billion, or 31%, compared to $2.1 billion for the prior year period. R&D expenses of $7.7 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 increased by $2.0 billion, or 34%, compared to $5.8 billion for the prior year period. The increase in both periods was primarily due to higher employee-related costs from an increase in headcount as we continue to expand our data center silicon, systems and software capabilities.

other_opex.text: All Other operating loss of $1.1 billion for the three months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 13% compared to All Other operating loss of $954 million for the prior year period. All Other operating loss of $3.2 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 increased by 9%, compared to All Other operating loss of $2.9 billion for the prior year period. The increase in both periods was primarily due to higher stock-based compensation expense as a result of higher headcount, partially offset by a lower amortization of acquisition-related intangibles.

nonop.heading: Interest Expense
nonop.text: Interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026 was $62 million and $136 million, respectively. Interest expense for the three and nine months ended September 27, 2025 was $37 million and $95 million, respectively. The increase for both periods was primarily due to the issuance of the August 2026 Notes, partially offset by the repayment of the $875 million aggregate principal amount of our 4.212% Senior Notes.

tax.heading: Income Taxes
tax.text:
We determine income taxes for interim reporting periods by applying our estimated annual effective tax rate to the year-to-date results and adjusted for tax items discrete to each period.

For the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026, we recorded an income tax benefit from continuing operations of $555 million and $65 million representing an effective tax rate of (29.6)% and (1.1)%, respectively. The tax benefit for both periods reflected the income tax benefit from foreign-derived deduction eligible income (FDDEI) and R&D tax credits. In addition, the tax benefit for the three and nine months ended September 26, 2026 also included a discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million and $918 million, respectively.

For the three and nine months ended September 27, 2025, we recorded an income tax provision from continuing operations of $153 million and an income tax benefit of $558 million representing an effective tax rate of 11.5% and (26.7)%, respectively. The tax provision (benefit) for both periods reflected the income tax benefit from foreign-derived intangible income (FDII) and R&D tax credits, partially offset by the tax rate detriment from foreign earnings, as well as a discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation.

net.text: Net income from discontinued operations for the nine months ended September 26, 2026 of $3 million included tax provision adjustments. Net income from discontinued operations for the three and nine months ended September 27, 2025 of $71 million and $175 million include the results of operations of the ZT Manufacturing Business, that was divested in October 2025. See Note 5 - Acquisitions and Divestitures in Part 1, Item 1 of this Form 10-Q.

capex.text: Net cash used in investing activities of continuing operations was $6.4 billion for the nine months ended September 26, 2026, which primarily consisted of purchases of short-term investments of $6.8 billion, purchases of property and equipment of $1.8 billion, and purchases of long-term investments of $1.1 billion, partially offset by $3.4 billion of proceeds from the maturity and sale of short-term investments. Net cash used in investing activities of discontinued operations was $0.2 billion, which represents payment for customary net working capital adjustments related to the divestiture of the ZT Manufacturing Business.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Short-term debt and commercial paper
lines.why: Borrowed money: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Income taxes payable, non-current
lines.why: Taxes on operating income due after a year (often uncertain tax positions): operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

Revenue recognized over time associated with custom products and development services accounted for approximately 9 %, 8 % and 25 % of the Company’s revenue in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
No customer accounted for at least 10% of the Company’s consolidated net revenue in fiscal years 2025 and 2024.
One Client and Gaming segment customer accounted for 18 % of consolidated net revenue in fiscal year 2023.

These products are incorporated into servers and other data center appliances sold by OEMs to the hyperscale customers or into custom servers or hardware designed by or for these customers and manufactured by ODMs or contract manufacturers.

The competitiveness of our products depends on a number of factors including, performance, total cost of ownership, timely product introductions, product quality and reliability, product features and capabilities, energy efficiency (including power consumption and battery life, given their impact on total cost of ownership), size (or form factor), selling price, cost, adherence to industry standards (and the creation of open industry standards), level of integration, software and hardware compatibility, ease of use and functionality of software design tools, completeness of applicable software
We rely on contracts and intellectual property rights to protect our products and technologies from unauthorized third-party copying and use.

• The success of our business depends on our ability to introduce products on a timely basis with features and performance levels that provide value to our customers while supporting significant industry transitions.

• We rely on third parties to manufacture our products, and if they are unable to do so on a timely basis in sufficient quantities and using competitive technologies, our business could be materially adversely affected.
• We depend on third-party companies for the design, manufacture and supply of motherboards, software, memory and other computer platform components to support our business and products.
• Our business depends on the proper functioning of our internal business processes and information systems.

The demand for such products will in part depend on the extent to which our customers utilize generative AI solutions in a wide variety of applications, and both the near-term and long-term trajectory of such generative AI solutions is unknown.

The success of our business depends on our ability to introduce products on a timely basis with features and performance levels that provide value to our customers while supporting and coinciding with significant industry transitions.

The demand for such products in part will depend on the extent to which our customers utilize generative AI solutions in a wide variety of applications as both the near-term and long-term trajectory of such generative AI solutions is unknown.
We also depend on the timing and success of our customers’ platform launches.

We depend on a small number of customers for a substantial portion of our business and we expect that a small number of customers will continue to account for a significant part of our revenue and receivables in the future.
Moreover, our key suppliers may reduce their output or become insolvent, thereby adversely impacting our ability to manufacture our products.

We rely on Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSMC) for the production of all wafers for microprocessor and GPU products at 7 nanometer (nm) or smaller nodes, and we rely primarily on GLOBALFOUNDRIES Inc. (GF) for wafers for microprocessor and GPU products manufactured at process nodes larger than 7 nm.
We also rely on third-party manufacturers to assemble, test, mark and pack (ATMP) our products.

Accordingly, we depend on these suppliers to allocate to us a portion of their manufacturing capacity sufficient to meet our needs, to produce products of acceptable quality and at acceptable manufacturing yields and to deliver those products to us on a timely basis and at acceptable prices.

We may purchase equipment, materials and substrates for use by our back-end manufacturing service providers from a number of suppliers and our operations depend upon obtaining deliveries of adequate supplies of equipment and materials of acceptable quality on a timely basis.
Our third-party suppliers also depend on the same timely delivery of adequate quantities of equipment and materials of acceptable quality in the manufacture of our products.
In addition, as many of our products increase in technical complexity, we rely on our third-party suppliers to update their processes in order to continue meeting our back-end manufacturing needs.
Certain equipment and materials that are used in the manufacture of our products are available only from a limited number of suppliers, or in some cases, a sole supplier.
We also depend on a limited number of suppliers to provide the majority of certain types of IC packages for our microprocessors, including our APU products.
Dependence on a sole supplier or a limited number of suppliers exacerbates these risks.
Moreover, we rely on TSMC, UMC and our other foundries to produce wafers with competitive performance attributes for our IC products.

As a result, our ability to generate revenue from our semi-custom products depends on our ability to secure customers for our semi-custom design pipeline, our customers’ desire to pursue the project and our semi-custom SoC products being incorporated into those customers’ products.
We may depend on vendors to create mitigations to their technology that we incorporate into our products and they may delay or decline to make such mitigations.
Our business relies on technology hardware, software, cloud services, infrastructure, networks and systems (collectively, IT Systems).
We own and manage some IT Systems but also rely on critical third-party IT Systems, products and services.
Sales of our MI308 products into China depend on customer demand, China’s import control rules and our ability to obtain licenses.

We depend on third-party companies for the design, manufacture and supply of motherboards, graphics cards, software (e.g., BIOS, operating systems, drivers, AI models or tools), memory and other components that we use to design, support and sell, and our customers utilize to support and/or use our product offerings.
We also rely on our AIB partners to support our products.

Our business depends on the proper functioning of our internal business processes and information systems and modification or interruption of such systems may disrupt our business, processes and internal controls.
We rely upon a number of internal business processes and information systems to support key business functions, and the efficient operation of these processes and systems is critical to our business.
Accordingly, we rely on our supply chain for the manufacturing, distribution and fulfillment of our products.

We rely on third-party providers to operate our regional product distribution centers and to manage the transportation of our work-in-process and finished products among our facilities, to our third-party manufacturers and to our customers.

In addition, we rely on third parties to provide certain information technology services to us, including help desk support, desktop application services, business and software support applications, server and storage administration, data center operations, database administration and voice, video and remote access.
